insight: Uzbekistan's performance during hydration breaks in the 2026 World Cup reveals some interesting trends. When they didn't press their opponents before a break, they were able to maintain a relatively stable pace, with a slight decrease in momentum of -0.020 minutes on average, which suggests that they were able to regroup and refocus during these breaks. However, when they did press before a break, they lost momentum at a much faster rate, with an average decrease of -0.100 minutes, and were unable to regain it afterwards, indicating that their high-intensity approach may have left them more vulnerable to counterattacks after the break. Overall, Uzbekistan's ability to gain momentum after hydration breaks was limited, with only half of the breaks resulting in a positive shift in momentum, highlighting the need for the team to adjust their strategy during these pauses in play.
